name: Iyongiyong
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Only wordlists exist per Glottolog (Decker & Abraham 2022 SIL wordlist; Blench 2014; Johnston 1919-22); no grammar or phonology of Iyongiyong/Bakpinka located

sources.citation: OLAC: resources in and about the Bakpinka language (bbs), as of 2024-12-01 (Internet Archive copy).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Catalog only: 3 items (Glottolog, Ethnologue, SIL 95078 = Decker et al. 2022). Confirms no other archived description.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Benard Abraham, Fittokka Gobak & Longdi Sylvanus. 2022. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Deko-Dusanga [uya], Iyongiyong [bbs], and Robambami [ibm] Languages in Cross River State, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2022-022. SIL International. 64 pp. (SIL archive 95078)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sect. 8.3 gives tentative consonant/vowel inventories (7 vowels + length) from a 222-item wordlist; Appendix E: 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' Wordlist is tone-marked; 'stress' and 'accent' 0 hits. Sect. 4.2 literature review names only Johnston 1919, Dimmendaal 1978, Wente-Lukas 1985, Blench 2020/2021 -- no phonology/grammar exists.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, John Muniru, David Onoja, Lewinan Andrew & Samuel Eju. 2022. A Sociolinguistic Profile of Five Upper Cross Language Varieties in Cross River State, Nigeria. JLSR 2022-023. SIL International.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Mentions Iyongiyong [bbs] only as a neighbouring language (Idoma village); nothing on its phonology.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2019/2020. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, ed. IV. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. Entry 36 Bakpinka.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; entry lists names (Iyongiyong, Uwet, Begbungba), classification Upper Cross East-West group, 'Said to be dying out', and 'Refs. Wordlist: Sterk (n.d.)' as the only reference.

sources.citation: Johnston, Harry H. 1919-1922. A Comparative Study of the Bantu and Semi-Bantu Languages, vols. 1-2. Oxford: Clarendon. Language 246 Uwet (archive.org scanned text).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; vocabulary columns, 'Prefixes in Uwet (246)', location note; vol. 2 remarks Uwet 'is more typically Semi-Bantu'. No accent remarks.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2014/2021. The Upper Cross languages: a comparative study. Unpublished ms., Cambridge, 189 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only other work with Iyongiyong data (Sterk's 312-item 'Iyɔŋiyɔŋ' wordlist) plus a general Upper Cross phonology overview (pp. ~7); may contain a family-level remark on tone/stress, though unlikely a Bakpinka-specific stress rule.
